subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should this PR be allowed to move toward merge after the `code_mode_exec` normalization repair, given that policy-active Codex turns will use unified exec and may start fresh threads on relay config drift?
rationale: The remaining choice affects tool-execution enforcement, existing Codex session continuity, and the runtime dependency boundary; automation can repair the missing mapping but cannot choose the security and compatibility tradeoff for maintainers.

options.title: Require normalization and runtime sign-off
options.body: Keep the PR draft or human-gated until `code_mode_exec` is normalized to `exec` and maintainers accept the current Codex runtime plus unified-exec/fresh-thread behavior.

options.title: Accept after mechanical repair
options.body: Allow the scoped relay fix to proceed once the mapping repair and focused tests land, accepting the compatibility risk for policy-active Codex users.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed alternative
options.body: Pause this positive-delivery path and route the cluster toward the narrower fail-closed behavior if maintainers do not want unified exec as the policy-active default.

recommendation.title: Require normalization and runtime sign-off
recommendation.body: Keep the PR draft or human-gated until `code_mode_exec` is normalized to `exec` and maintainers accept the current Codex runtime plus unified-exec/fresh-thread behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a maintainer-level security and compatibility tradeoff, and steipete is the strongest current maintainer routing signal in the touched area.
